sources.entry: Filestash - Web file manager that lets you manage your data anywhere it is located: FTP, SFTP, WebDAV, Git, S3, Minio, Dropbox, or Google Drive. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker
Filestash | Web file manager for FTP, SFTP, S3, WebDAV and more

summary.one_liner: Filestash is a web-based file manager that connects to many storage backends (SFTP, S3, SMB, WebDAV, FTP, NFS, IPFS and others) and is extended through a plugin architecture.
summary.what_it_does: Filestash provides a browser-based file manager with a handcrafted vanilla JS web client that works across many storage protocols, including SFTP, S3, SMB, WebDAV, IPFS, FTP and NFS. The core is built around storage, authentication, authorisation, search and other interfaces, and most functionality lives in plugins. Plugins can be written in Rust or Go (compiled in), or added as runtime plugins: a zip with frontend changes and WebAssembly code that runs in a sandboxed VM with restricted permissions. The README also describes a workflow engine that chains actions on file events (such as Slack or email notifications), a set of file-type apps (for example previewers for photography, CAD, GIS, and scientific formats), and APIs and gateways that re-expose data over protocols like SFTP, S3, FTP and WebDAV. Other listed features include versioning, audit, antivirus, quota, public sharing site, and optional AI search and OCR. Native sync clients for desktop and Android are mentioned as separate projects.
use_cases: browse and manage files on an SFTP or FTP server from a browser
web access to S3 or MinIO buckets
web front end for WebDAV or SMB file shares
sync files across devices with a native client
expose storage over SFTP, S3, FTP or WebDAV via gateways
automate file workflows with notifications or pipelines
preview specialised file formats such as CAD, GIS or scientific data
how_to_run: Standard installation procedure is described in the project's documentation guide (linked from the README)
notable: Plugin-driven core: storage, auth, authorisation and other components are replaceable plugins
Runtime plugins distributed as zip files with WebAssembly code running in a permission-restricted VM
Connects to many storage protocols from one web interface
Workflow engine chaining actions on file events, from notifications to MFT pipelines
Large set of file-type apps for photography, astronomy, GIS, 3D, embroidery and more
caveats: Code is the only way to extend it; the README states there are no no-code options
Commercial users are pointed to a paid support contract
Native sync clients are separate repositories rather than part of this one
